result.title: Subliminal Learning in Vision-Language Models
result.summary: Subliminal learning is a phenomenon in large language models (LLMs) where a teacher passes a hidden preference to a student through training data unrelated to that preference. We study whether subliminal learning also occurs in vision-language models (VLMs). We finetune a teacher VLM to prefer a specific animal or facial attribute and use a control teacher from the same base model. Both teachers generate numbers for an unrelated visual task involving geometric shapes. Two students initialized from the same base VLM are finetuned on the same images, using numbers generated by either the biased or control teacher. Across VLMs ranging from 2B to 7B parameters, we find that both animal and facial preferences can transfer through this unrelated task. Students trained on biased-teacher outputs select the target more often than control students, with a difference of up to $\sim$10 percentage points in the animal preference task. Transfer can become stronger with more training data and varies with the target preference, model, and how the numbers are generated. Beyond preferences, we show that the biased student's explanations use more of the same words and phrases as the biased teacher's explanations than those of the control student, even when all three models select the same image. These results matter for training VLMs and show that training on unrelated data may change both a VLM's image preferences and how it explains its choices, and that transfer can become stronger with more training samples.

AI.brief_summary: 在 2B–7B 的 VLM 中微调 teacher 使其偏好某种动物或面部属性，让其在与该偏好无关的几何图形任务上生成数字，再用这些数字微调同源 student，检验隐藏偏好是否迁移，并比较 student 解释用词与 biased teacher 的重合度。
AI.relevance_reason: 「控制教师 + 无关任务输出」的对照设计可供核查 LVR 中用教师轨迹或推理数据训练时，监督信号是否夹带与任务无关的隐藏属性或被 latent 状态吸收；其对答案选择与解释文本的分层评测也提示需区分表述变化与内部状态的实际改变。
